sources.citation: Zheltov, Alexander. 2020. Plurality marking in Leko and Yendang groups (Adamawa, Niger-Congo) with some reference to noun classification. Language in Africa 1(3): 125-154. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-125-154.
sources.note: Nothing about Yotti; Yoti/Yotti appears only in the group listing (p. 126: 'Yendang (with Kusheki, Yoti)') and in Appendix 2 (Glottolog tree, p. 150). Its tone remarks (p. 129 'the tonal notation needs to be specified'; p. 135 'absence of tone marking indicates middle tone') concern Maya (Bali) and Nyong, not Yotti. Useful mainly for the reference list, which gives the URL of the Blench wordlist and the St Petersburg field data on Yendang/Waka/Kugama.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue 22nd ed., entry 'Yotti' (Wayback capture 2019 of ethnologue.com/language/yot).
sources.note: Nothing visible; free part gives classification and alternate names 'Wonkorok, Yoti'; population/typology paywalled.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-150 (submitter Zachariah Yoder, Language Development Facilitators, 2011-08-29; adopted 2012-02-03): split [yen] Yendang into [ynq] Yendang and [yot] Yotti; with the accompanying Request for New Language Code Element for Yotti.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Gives sociolinguistic facts only: autonym Wɔ̀nkoɾɔk, 8 villages 2-15 km south of Mayo-Lope (Taraba State), ~3000-5000 speakers, intelligibility test with Yendang text 'very poor', lexical similarity 35% Bali, 35% Kpasham, 13% Yendang; 'What written literature... exist in this language?: None known.' Only published source cited: Blench 2011 Atlas of Nigerian Languages.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. n.d. [file dated 2013-08-30; cited as Blench 2009 by Zheltov 2020]. The Maya [Yendang] languages: Wordlists collected by Barau Kato and Zachariah Yoder, analysis by Roger Blench. Unpublished ms., 15 pp. (Glottolog ref 158487).
sources.note: Nothing. It is a four-language comparative wordlist (Ɓali, Kpaʃam, Yoti, Yandaŋ) with an etymological commentary column; Yoti forms carry tone diacritics (e.g. ɲã́ tíî 'forehead', kɔ̀kɔ̀bíli 'skin', gbɔ̀ ̃ 'locust bean') but there is no phonology section, no statement on tone inventory and no mention of stress or accent. Introduction (p. ii): 'Little has been published on these languages and nothing at all on Yoti... no evidence has been available until present to situate Yoti.'
